discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: two-dimensional materials and superconductivity
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that twisting two graphene layers by about 1.1 degrees makes the electronic bands nearly flat, so that electron interactions dominate. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group confirmed this experimentally. Using a simple stacking technique with controlled rotation, they showed that magic-angle bilayer graphene is a correlated insulator and becomes superconducting when gated. The two papers started the field of twistronics. Since then, laboratories around the world have used the twist angle as a tuning knob for correlated insulators, unconventional superconductivity, orbital magnetism, the fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect in moiré materials, and many related phenomena, all in a single tunable device made of carbon alone. This is the kind of simple, bold experiment that turns long-standing theoretical questions about strongly correlated and unconventional superconductivity into something any well-equipped van der Waals laboratory can study. Its impact on condensed matter physics has been broad and lasting.
